messages.subject: CFA and SEM command
parts:
hello,

I am running a command and it won't work :(.
I am not used of working with R (lavaan), but the command already did what it had to do ones...
Whatever I try the same errors comes back.

> cfa.model = '
+ interperq =~ IP1 + IP2 + IP3 + IP4 + IP5 + IP6 + IP7 + IP8 + IP9 + IP10 + IP11
+ techq =~ TQ1 + TQ2 + TQ3 + TQ4 + TQ5 + TQ6
+ enviromq =~ EQ1 + EQ2 + EQ3 + EQ4 +EQ5 +EQ6 +EQ7 + EQ8 + EQ9 +EQ10 +EQ11
+ admq =~ AQ2 + AQ3 + AQ4 + AQ5 + AQ6 + AQ7 + AQ8 + AQ9
+ wt =~ WT23 + WT1 + WT2r + WT3r + WT4r + WT5r + WT7r + WT8r + WT9r + WT10
+ pt =~ PT1 + PT2 + PT3 + PT4 + PT5 + PT6 
+ bi =~ BI1 +B12 + BI3 + BI4 + BI5
+ he =~ HE1 + HE2 + HE3 + HE4 + HE5 + HE6
+ quallife =~ QLA1 + QLA2'
> fit = sem(cfa.model, data=voor_R)
Error in sem(cfa.model, data = voor_R) : could not find function "sem"  (also with cfa of CFA instead of sem)
> summary(fit, fit.measure=TRUE, standardized=TRUE)
Error in summary(fit, fit.measure = TRUE, standardized = TRUE) : 
  object 'fit' not found

Anybody who can help?

messages.author: 6f81c58ba9ed02c3
messages.subject: Re: CFA and SEM command
parts:
Hello,

Did you load the lavaan package when you opened R? This message usually displays if the package hasn't been loaded because the software doesn't know what the command means. So before running this model, you would want to run library(lavaan).

Best,

Ryan

messages.author: 6f81c58ba9ed02c3
messages.subject: Re: CFA and SEM command
parts:
Hi Melissa,

Every time you open R you have to re-load the packages you've downloaded. So, once you run this command:

library(lavaan)

R will recognize all of the commands that are contained in that package. This should take care of your error.

Best,

Ryan
